cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Vertical scaling (scale-up) gives one server more CPU, memory and faster disks. Horizontal scaling (scale-out) adds servers: read replicas for reads and sharding for writes and data size.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Vertical is simple, needs no code changes and keeps transactions easy, but has a hard ceiling, rising cost and stays a single point of failure. Horizontal removes the ceiling and adds fault tolerance but brings replication lag, cross-shard queries, rebalancing and operational complexity. Usually optimize and scale up first.

questions.q: Do read replicas scale every workload horizontally?
questions.a: Only reads. Every replica still applies every write and the primary accepts all of them.

questions.q: Name two frictions of vertical scaling.
questions.a: Hard hardware ceiling and an exponential cost curve; it is also a single point of failure.

questions.q: What is a common horizontal scaling risk?
questions.a: Bad shard keys causing hotspots, and painful resharding at scale.
